Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

The domain-scoped element-hiding rule iafcertsearch.org#⁠#⁠[⁠class*="cookie-consent-banner"]⁠ removed the sheet and backdrop and left the page intact and fully usable in the locked AdGuard CLI filtering session. ## Rule `iafcertsearch.org##[class*="cookie-consent-banner"]` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice (page-owned annoyance), not first-party advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall and not a scam/phishing page, so none of the instruction's closing rules applies. No maintainer rule blocks a cosmetic hide here:⁠ the consent sheet is hidden and the page afterwards works (content legible, no scroll lock, no popup return). No existing shared rule family covers this consent UI, so a new domain-scoped rule in the Cookie Notices filter is the appropriate fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

issue.title: Remove AI filters from the Other Annoyances
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

AdGuard Other Annoyances filter blocks AI features such as Google Search Overview.

### Proposed solution

Since AdGuard already offers an AI-annoyance blocking filter list (Stevo's AI Blocklist) I think that rules blocking AI should be removed from the Other Annoyances filter list. Additionally, while the filter provides many useful rules that block unnecessary clutter and other features, some users use these AI features and don't want them blocked, but still want the blocking power of the rest of the filter list. All in all, I think this should be done because there is already a specialized list for this specific purpose that is more comprehensive, and some users want to enable Other Annoyances without blocking AI features.

### Additional information

_No response_
